card.name: Qualifier words inside dosing instructions
card.fires_on: Adjectives or participles that qualify a dose, rate, range or duration in dosing text, such as specific, recommended, scheduled, appropriate and consistent (with). It fires just before the thing being qualified or the 'with' phrase.

modes.label: Specific/recommended before range or rate
modes.description: A qualifier sits right before a range or rate in dose adjustment text.
modes.example: TSH above normal trimester-<< specific>> range Pre-pregnancy dosage may increase

modes.label: Consistent with treatment goals
modes.description: The word 'consistent' follows 'shortest duration' in prescribing advice.
modes.example: at the lowest effective dose and the shortest duration<< consistent>> with treatment goals and risks for the individual

modes.label: Scheduled or age-appropriate dosing
modes.description: A qualifier before time or amount in dose instructions.
modes.example: Resume dosing at the next regularly<< scheduled>> time. 2.3 Dosage

card.writes: It seems to push the next word away from example-style lists and toward the plain noun the qualifier modifies.
card.plain: It marks describing words in dosing directions, like specific, recommended or consistent, that come just before the dose noun.
